The device simulator is a stdlib-only Python fake Moonraker server at `tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py` (landed on `jusprin-newui` 2026-09-08 as ecf13456bc + a25b95fb39; pointer in agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md), with `/sim` control and log endpoints and `--install-preset`, which writes a user printer preset (`host_type=moonraker`, `print_host=127.0.0.1:7125`, `printhost_port=7125`, `printer_agent=moonraker`, inherits `MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle`) and selects it in `JusPrin2.conf`. Two earlier in-process `FakePrinterAgent` attempts were reverted (commits a162493544 and 3c244108b4) because they never drove the UI and needed upstream edits; Kenneth explicitly preferred an independent fake Moonraker.

Verified in the real app: the Print button path (`Moonraker::test` → upload → `/printer/print/start`) sent the sliced cube's G-code to the simulator. The Moonraker printer agent's startup connect (`MachineObject::connect(use_openssl)`, called from `DeviceCore/DevManager.cpp:532,556`) uses the `enable_ssl_for_mqtt` app-config flag (default true), so it dials `https://127.0.0.1:7125` and fails with "SSL connect error" until that flag is `false`; a separate session is fixing that.

On 2026-09-08 Kenneth asked for the "Not connected" line to be fixed. Three changes on the branch: `MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp` `#if 0` → `#if 1` (status query + websocket stream; upstream/main still has `#if 0`, merge-tree clean), `SetupCommands::printer_connection` reports state for any print host whose machine dev_id matches the preset's host (Bambu gate removed, `monitor_available` only for Bambu), and the menu row stays enabled with no monitor icon. The simulator gained a websocket (`identify`, `subscribe`, `notify_status_update` every second). Screenshots of the rebuilt app showed Idle, Printing, and Offline (about 30 s after the simulator went away), and the agent re-subscribed when the simulator returned (backoff up to ten attempts). The shell's Print button also has its own gate (`StatusRow::request_action`: "Printer connection required" unless Bambu or a non-empty `print_host`), which passes for the fake preset; Kenneth hit it because opening a saved 3mf switched him to MyKlipper.

A user preset whose `version` does not parse is silently skipped at load, so the installer copies the Custom vendor's version.

The header chip names the printer by `printer_model`. The first installer left it inherited, so the chip read "Generic Klipper Printer" and Kenneth read that as "no printer found" (2026-09-08); the installer now writes `printer_model: "Fake Moonraker"`, which is safe because process compatibility keys on the parent preset name, not the model. Never launch a test instance on his screen while he is at the keyboard: he closed one mid-test. The chip's menu has no preset picker (only nozzle variants, "Printer settings…", "Add a printer…"), so selection happens through `presets.machine` in `JusPrin2.conf`, which the app rewrites on exit: install the preset only while the app is closed.

**Why:** Kenneth wants to test sending G-code and querying status without hardware, for agents and by hand; the simplest route is the real HTTP path, not a C++ double.

**How to apply:** Run the simulator, install the preset with the app closed, launch with a scratch `--datadir`, and read `GET /sim/log`. For the agent connect, set `app.enable_ssl_for_mqtt` to false in the scratch conf. See [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]] for pressing Print headlessly.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

# Fake printer for testing without hardware

`fake_moonraker.py` is a stand-alone Moonraker (Klipper) printer written in
plain Python. JusPrin talks to it through the same network code it uses for a
real Klipper printer, so tests exercise the app's real upload, print, and
status paths. It answers the endpoints JusPrin actually calls and adds a
`/sim` control API so a person or an AI agent can change the printer's state
and read back what the app sent.

Moonraker was chosen over Bambu because Bambu printers speak to a closed
network plugin over MQTT with TLS plus FTPS, while Moonraker is plain HTTP and
a websocket. Only the standard library is used, and the tests run in about
ten seconds:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/printer_sim -v
```

## What it simulates

| JusPrin code | What the simulator answers |
|---|---|
| Print button (`src/slic3r/Utils/Moonraker.cpp`) | `GET /server/info`, `GET /server/files/roots`, `POST /server/files/upload`, `POST /printer/print/start` |
| Moonraker printer agent (`src/slic3r/Utils/MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp`) | `GET /server/info` on connect, `GET /printer/objects/query`, `GET /printer/objects/list`, `ws://…/websocket` (`server.connection.identify`, `printer.objects.subscribe`, `notify_status_update` once a second), `POST /printer/gcode/script`, `GET /server/database/item?namespace=lane_data` (AFC filament lanes) |

A started print heats up and progresses to 100 % on its own over
`--print-seconds` (default 60). The G-code interpreter understands `G28`,
`M104`/`M109`, `M140`/`M190`, `M106`/`M107`, `SET_HEATER_TEMPERATURE`,
`TURN_OFF_HEATERS`, `PAUSE`, `RESUME`, `CANCEL_PRINT`, `SDCARD_PRINT_FILE`,
`M112` and `FIRMWARE_RESTART`; everything else is accepted and logged.

## Control API

Everything under `/sim` is the simulator's own, not Moonraker's.

| Request | Effect |
|---|---|
| `GET /sim` | Printer state (`state`, `klippy_state`, `filename`, `progress`, `extruder`, `heater_bed`, `fan`, `offline`), uploaded `files`, and the last 50 log entries |
| `POST /sim` with JSON | Change state; returns the new state. Unknown keys are rejected so typos do not pass silently |
| `GET /sim/log` | Every request the app made, oldest first: `time`, `method`, `path`, one-line `summary` |
| `DELETE /sim/log` | Clear the log between steps |
| `GET /server/files/gcodes/<name>` | Download a file the app uploaded |

Keys accepted by `POST /sim`: `state` (`standby`, `printing`, `paused`,
`complete`, `cancelled`, `error`), `klippy_state` (`ready`, `startup`,
`shutdown`, `error`, `disconnected`), `filename`, `progress` (0 to 1),
`extruder_temp`, `extruder_target`, `bed_temp`, `bed_target`, `fan` (0 to 1),
`homed`, `message`, `offline` (true makes the printer stop answering, the
websocket included), `auto` (false freezes heating and progress), `lanes`
(replaces the AFC filament lanes), `clear_log`, `reset`.

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"state":"printing","filename":"benchy.gcode","progress":0.42}'
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"state":"paused"}'
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"klippy_state":"shutdown"}'
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"offline":true}'
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"reset":true}'
```

## What JusPrin shows

Open the printer half of the header chip. The first row of its menu is the
printer name with the connection state, computed by
`SetupCommands::printer_connection` from the status the agent receives:

| Simulator | Menu row |
|---|---|
| running, no print | **Idle** |
| running a print, started from JusPrin or with `POST /sim {"state":"printing"}` | **Printing** |
| stopped, or `POST /sim {"offline":true}` | **Offline**, about 30 seconds after the last status |
| the selected preset has no print host | **Not connected** |

The chip itself reads **Fake Moonraker · 0.4**. A few seconds after launch the
agent connects, reads the initial status, and opens the websocket. If the
simulator goes away the agent retries with growing delays (1 s, 2 s, 4 s, up
to ten attempts); restart the simulator within a few minutes and the row
returns to Idle on its own. After ten failed attempts, reselect the printer.

## Setup, once

JusPrin's shell hides the dialog that would let you type a print host, so the
simulator installs the printer preset. With JusPrin **closed**:

```bash
python3 tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py --install-preset
```

This writes `user/default/machine/Fake Moonraker 0.4 nozzle.json` into the
JusPrin data directory (`~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` on macOS,
`~/.config/JusPrin2` on Linux, `%APPDATA%\JusPrin2` on Windows) and selects it
as the current printer. The preset inherits the `MyKlipper 0.4 nozzle` system
preset from the Custom vendor (`--inherits` picks another installed Klipper
preset, `--datadir` another data directory, `--port` another port). JusPrin
rewrites its config on exit and the chip's menu has no preset picker, so an
installer run while the app is open is lost.

One current limitation: the agent dials `https://` while the app setting
`enable_ssl_for_mqtt` is true, which is the default, and then fails with an
SSL connect error in the app log. Until that is fixed in the app, set it to
false in `JusPrin2.conf` (with the app closed):

```bash
python3 -c "import json,os; p=os.path.expanduser('~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf'); c=json.load(open(p)); c.setdefault('app',{})['enable_ssl_for_mqtt']='false'; json.dump(c,open(p,'w'),indent='\t',ensure_ascii=False)"
```

The installer does not change this setting itself because it also governs
Bambu printers' LAN connections.

## Manual test: printer status

1. Start the simulator and leave the terminal open:
   `python3 tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py`
2. Start JusPrin. Within a few seconds the simulator prints `server info`,
   `status query`, `websocket connected`, and `subscribe: …`.
3. Click the printer half of the chip. The first row reads **Fake Moonraker ·
   Idle**. Click elsewhere to close the menu.
4. In another terminal: `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"state":"printing","filename":"benchy.gcode","progress":0.4}'`.
   Reopen the menu: **Printing**.
5. `curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim -d '{"state":"complete"}'`.
   Reopen the menu: **Idle**.
6. Press Ctrl+C in the simulator's terminal. Wait 30 seconds, reopen the menu:
   **Offline**.
7. Start the simulator again. Within about a minute the menu is back to
   **Idle**, and the simulator has printed a new `websocket connected` line.

## Manual test: sending a print

1. With the simulator running, import a model file into JusPrin (drag an STL
   in, or use the Import button). Do not open a saved 3mf project: a project
   carries its own printer preset and switches away from the fake printer.
2. Press **Slice**, then **Print**, then **Upload and Print** in the dialog.
3. The simulator prints four lines: storage roots, server info, the upload
   with its byte count, and the print start. Reopen the chip menu:
   **Printing**. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7125/sim` shows the filename and
   the progress climbing to 1.0 over a minute, after which the menu says
   **Idle** again.

## Automated test (AI agent or script)

1. Start the simulator on a free port with a short print, quiet:
   `python3 tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py --port 7135 --print-seconds 5 --quiet &`
2. Copy the JusPrin data directory to a scratch folder, clear
   `recent_projects` in its `JusPrin2.conf`, set `enable_ssl_for_mqtt` to
   `"false"` (see above), and install the preset into it:
   `python3 tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py --install-preset --datadir <dir> --port 7135`
3. Launch the built app against it with a model, and give the agent runtime a
   dummy key so it does not open a Keychain prompt:
   `OPENAI_API_KEY=x <app>/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <dir> tests/data/20mm_cube.obj &`
4. Connection check: within about 10 seconds `GET /sim/log` contains
   `/server/info`, `/printer/objects/query`, `websocket connected`, and a
   `subscribe:` entry. The app's own log under `<dir>/log/` contains
   `MoonrakerPrinterAgent: connect_printer completed`.
5. Print check: slice and send (see below), then assert that `GET /sim/log`
   ends with `/server/files/upload` and `/printer/print/start`, and that
   `GET /sim` reports `"state": "printing"` with the uploaded filename. Fetch
   the file back with `GET /server/files/gcodes/<name>` to inspect the
   G-code the app produced.
6. State checks: `POST /sim` with `offline`, `state`, temperatures, or
   progress, and read the app's reaction from its log or from screenshots of
   the chip menu (the desktop-control tools can open it with a click on the
   printer half of the chip once the app is frontmost).

On macOS the app can be driven without a screen by posting key events to its
process. This also works while the Mac is locked, where screenshot tools are
refused; mouse events are not delivered that way:

```bash
swiftc -O -o /tmp/mac_post_key tests/printer_sim/mac_post_key.swift
PID=$(pgrep -f "OrcaSlicer --datadir <dir>")
/tmp/mac_post_key $PID 15 cmd            # Cmd+R: slice the plate
sleep 12
/tmp/mac_post_key $PID 5 cmd shift       # Cmd+Shift+G: open the send dialog
sleep 4
/tmp/mac_post_key $PID 48                # Tab: focus the Upload button
/tmp/mac_post_key $PID 124               # Right: move to Upload and Print
/tmp/mac_post_key $PID 49                # Space: press it
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:7135/sim/log    # expect server info, upload, print start
```

This is the sequence that verified the whole path on 2026-09-07 and
2026-09-08: the app checked `/server/info`, uploaded the sliced cube (about
340 KB), started the print, and the chip menu showed Idle, Printing, and
Offline as the simulator's state changed.

## Known limits

- Opening a saved project switches to the printer stored in it. Import a
  model file instead, or pick the fake preset again under "Printer settings…".
- The websocket speaks only the methods the agent uses and pushes the full
  subscribed objects every second rather than diffs.
- No authentication and no Happy Hare `mmu` object.
- `mac_post_key.swift` is macOS only; on Linux and Windows drive the app with
  a desktop-automation tool.

**How it works, on that branch:**

It answers the same HTTP/websocket endpoints the real Moonraker printer code in JusPrin calls — `GET /server/info`, file upload, `/printer/print/start`, the objects-query/subscribe websocket — so JusPrin talks to it through its real networking code, not a stub inside the app.
2. It adds a `/sim` control API on top: `POST /sim` lets you set printer state (`printing`, `paused`, `offline`, temperatures, progress, etc.), and `GET /sim/log` shows every request JusPrin actually made, so you can verify behavior without touching real hardware.

6. Two earlier attempts at this (building a fake printer agent *inside* the C++ app) were tried and reverted (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`) because they bypassed the real network code and needed upstream registration — the standalone-server approach is what stuck.

Here's how the two branches relate: one is literally a subset of the other — same commits, not a fork with different changes.

**The short version:** `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` and `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` share the exact same commit history, all the way up through the last fake-printer commit. `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` then has three more commits on top that have nothing to do with the fake printer — they're separate UI styling work. So there's no meaningful diff between them on the fake-printer feature itself; it's identical in both.

**The fuller picture, in order:**

1. All three branches you might care about — your current `jusprin-newui`, plus these two — share a common starting point at commit `56eb9a1a46` ("Fail the Windows build script when a step fails"), dated 2026-09-07.

2. From that point, `jusprin-newui` (what you're on now) went off and did unrelated work — things like the MCP tool catalog changes and moving the Agent's OpenAI key into AppConfig. It never got the fake-printer commits.

3. Separately, `claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78` branched off that same point and did the fake-printer work: first a false start (`a162493544`, reverted by `3b14c705a5`), a second false start (`3c244108b4`, reverted by `1408ee3a16`), then the version that stuck — `ecf13456bc` (the Python simulator) and `a25b95fb39` (the C++ side that reports live printer status). That last commit, `a25b95fb39`, is the tip of this branch.

4. `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` contains every single one of those same commits — it's not a copy, it's the identical git history, meaning at some point someone pointed a new branch name at that same commit (or built directly on top of it). ----- a162493544 -----
Add a fake printer agent for testing without hardware

Printer status and print-job code paths previously could not be
exercised at all without a physical printer connected: every
IPrinterAgent implementation in the tree talks to real hardware or a
real network endpoint, and no test covered any of them.

FakePrinterAgent is an IPrinterAgent implementation backed by a scripted
status sequence instead of a real MQTT/LAN connection. It replays a
canned "connect -> heat -> print -> finish" timeline, pushing the same
Bambu-style push_status JSON a real printer sends through the same
callbacks, so code downstream of the interface cannot tell the
difference.

It can be driven two ways:

- Automated, from test code: connect_printer(), start_local_print() and
  push_status() are called directly. Three Catch2 cases cover full
  scenario replay, single-status injection, and cancellation.
- Manually, by a person: setting JUSPRIN_FAKE_PRINTER_CONSOLE=1 starts a
  numbered menu on stdin for connecting, replaying the scenario, and
  jumping to named presets (Idle, Heating, Printing 25%/75%, Finished,
  Failed). Nothing to memorize and no parameters to type.

Registration follows the existing pattern exactly: one register_agent<T>
line, the same way every other printer agent is discovered. The registry
is bootstrapped by an explicit list rather than self-registering statics,
so a new implementation still needs that line. Total footprint outside
the two new files is four lines.

Scope limit worth knowing: this exercises the IPrinterAgent layer only.
It does not touch MoonrakerPrinterAgent or the PrintHost family, which
speak real wire protocols and remain untested. It also has no visible
effect in the JusPrin shell today, which hides the sidebar and tab strip
and contains no reference to MachineObject, so no screen in this branch
renders the resulting status for a non-Bambu printer.

----- 3c244108b4 -----
Let the fake printer drive the header printer chip

The chip's connection line (Not connected / Offline / Idle / Printing) is
the only field in the printer and spool menus that comes from a printer
rather than from presets, and it reported state for Bambu printers only.
That left the fake printer agent with nothing to drive, and no way to
switch it on either: the Physical Printer dialog is the only UI exposing
the printer_agent and print_host fields it needs, and this shell hides
the sidebar that opens it.

Three changes:

- The chip also reports live state when the active printer agent is the
  simulator. Gated on the agent rather than on "not Bambu", so every real
  printer keeps its current behaviour, including the deliberate "not
  connected" shown for other print hosts.
- Setting JUSPRIN_FAKE_PRINTER installs the simulator and registers and

  variable now starts the manual console, which previously had its own.
- switch_printer_agent() leaves the simulator installed while that

device stays FAKE001 and both the automatic connect and a status pushed
from the console reach MachineObject::parse_json, which is what feeds the
chip. With it unset, no device is registered, no console starts, and the
agent switches to orca exactly as before.

Add a fake Moonraker printer for testing without hardware

Nothing in the tree could exercise sending a print or reading printer
status without a physical printer. Two earlier attempts built a fake
IPrinterAgent inside the app; both were reverted because they bypassed
every line of real network code and needed upstream registration.

tests/printer_sim/fake_moonraker.py is a stand-alone Moonraker (Klipper)
printer in plain Python, standard library only. JusPrin reaches it through
its real Moonraker code: the Print button's server check, upload and
print-start requests, and the printer agent's connect, status query and
websocket stream (identify, subscribe, notify_status_update). A started
print heats up and progresses on its own; a small G-code interpreter
handles the commands the agent sends. A /sim control API sets the
printer's state (printing, paused, offline, temperatures, Klipper down)
and returns a log of every request the app made, which is what a person
or an AI agent asserts on.

--install-preset writes a user printer preset pointing at the simulator
(printer_model "Fake Moonraker", so the header chip names it) and selects
it in the app config. It copies the vendor's version string because a
preset whose version does not parse is silently skipped at load.

mac_post_key.swift posts key events to the app's process so an agent can
slice and press Print without a screen; this also works while the Mac is
locked, where screenshot tools are refused.

Moonraker.cpp and MoonrakerPrinterAgent.cpp. Verified against the built
app twice: it uploaded the sliced cube and started the print, and the
simulator ran it to completion. The README carries the manual and the
agent procedures, and engineering-method.md points at it.

printer: SetupCommands::printer_connection returned early unless the
preset used the Bambu network, and the Moonraker agent never received

own web page instead, so their native panel never needed the data).

state for any preset with a print host, provided the machine's dev_id
matches that host; a preset without a host, such as one restored from a
saved 3mf, stays "Not connected" even though the previous machine is
still selected in the device manager. monitor_available is true only for
Bambu, since Orca's monitor tab knows nothing else, and the menu row
stays enabled without the monitor icon when there is a state to show.

# Fake Bambu printer — what landed, why, commits, how to use

This is an **in-process stand-in for Bambu’s closed network plugin**. It is not a fake printer on the wire (no MQTT, FTPS, or discovery). With a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected, JusPrin’s Bambu UI paths — printer-menu Idle / Printing / Offline, Select Machine, and Send print job — run without hardware.

The operator guide in the tree is `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

---

## Why

Two earlier attempts were reverted because they looked like a fake printer but never entered the Bambu UI:

| Commit | What it did | Why it failed |
|---|---|---|
| `a162493544` | `FakePrinterAgent` under its **own** agent id, plus a non-Bambu preset | Every Bambu-only gate (`is_bbl_vendor()`, Select Machine, print job) rejected it |
| `3c244108b4` | Special-cased the header chip so the fake could show Idle / Printing / Offline | Patched a symptom. Kenneth reverted both because nothing visible worked |

A separate Moonraker/Klipper simulator already exists on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` (`tests/printer_sim/`). That fakes the **print-host** HTTP/websocket path. Bambu is a different agent (`"bbl"` wrapping `libbambu_networking`). Faking Bambu’s network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and rejected.

Kenneth’s decisions for this work: emulate **A1 mini (`N1`)**, control surface is a **JSON file only** (no MCP tools), keep the Moonraker simulator for Klipper.

---

## Design that actually works

Keep a **real Bambu system preset** selected so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true. Then substitute the fake **only at the printer-agent factory**, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`.

The one upstream seam is three additive lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp`). No upstream line was deleted or rewritten:

```3574:3579:src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp
    if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor()) {
        effective_agent_id = BBL_PRINTER_AGENT_ID;
        cloud_agent_id = BBL_CLOUD_PROVIDER;
        // Fork policy: fake mode substitutes the Bambu agent. Additive; no upstream line deleted.
        if (const std::string fake_id = fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config); !fake_id.empty())
            effective_agent_id = fake_id;
```

If `is_bbl_vendor()` is false, this branch never runs and the agent stays `orca` or `moonraker`. That is why an embedded 3mf preset named “Bambu Lab A1 mini …” is not enough: BBL vendor files must be installed under `<datadir>/system/`.

The fake implements `IPrinterAgent`. It announces device `FAKE001` via the same SSDP-style JSON the Moonraker agent uses, then `DeviceManager` creates a `MachineObject`. Status is a Bambu `push_status` heartbeat about once a second. Offline is “stop pushing”; after ~30 s (`DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`) the menu first row is Offline.

Heartbeat does **not** start in the constructor. Tests that never call `set_queue_on_main_fn` stay quiet. The GUI always sets that callback last, which is when the heartbeat starts.

---

## What shipped

Fork-owned agent:

- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.hpp`
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp`
- Wired in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`

Behavior:

- Registers as `jusprin-fake-bambu` via `NetworkAgentFactory::register_printer_agent`
- Reads `jusprin.fake_printer` from AppConfig (JSON boolean stored as the string `"true"`)
- Control file: `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json`, reread ~1s
- Printer type `N1`; Select Machine lists **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**
- `start_local_print` logs the filename. With no control file it replays a canned idle→print scenario. With a control file, send still succeeds and the file’s state wins
- After SSDP, queues access codes then `MonitorPanel::select_machine` / `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine` on the main thread

Tests: `tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`, target `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (GUI build). Announce JSON, control-file parsing, agent id, canned scenario. They do not start the heartbeat unless the test sets `set_queue_on_main_fn`.

Docs pointers: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `engineering-method.md`, `orca-integration-guide.md` §4.

The planning handoff `agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md` was never committed and was deleted after the work landed. It was stale (“not started”) and contradicted the operator README.

E2E on 2026-09-08 (scratch `FakeBambuTest.app`, isolated datadir): log showed `jusprin-fake-bambu` and `set_selected_machine=FAKE001`; menu Idle → Printing via control file → Offline after `"offline":true`; Cmd+R slice; Cmd+Shift+G send listed the fake LAN machine and completed with `start_local_print` in the log.

Authored on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7`, then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (one CMake conflict: keep both `shell_theme_tests` and `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests`). Both cherry-picks are on `origin/jusprin-newui`.

| Operator docs | `ca7e517000` | `e04c0d40d3` | Document how to operate the fake Bambu printer for humans and agents |

`7acf075aaa` is the one to cite on the production branch. Bodies:

- Implementation: keep a real Bambu preset selected and swap the closed plugin for `FakeBambuAgent` so header menu, Select Machine, and print job can run without a printer. (~1253 lines: agent, 4-line `GUI_App` seam, initial README, Catch2 tests, engineering-method pointer.)
- Docs: the first README used INI config and treated the chip as the status surface. The follow-up records JSON config, a real Bambu **system** preset, isolated-instance rules, and the printer-menu first row.

Cherry-pick parent of `7acf075aaa` is `367f5703b3` (then-tip of `jusprin-newui`). The worktree commits sat on `a9adaae973` (token-scale guards), which is why they were cherry-picked rather than merged.

---

## How to use it

Canonical steps: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

### 1. Isolated datadir

Quit JusPrin. The app rewrites `JusPrin2.conf` on exit. Use a **scratch** `--datadir`, not the everyday config.

If another JusPrin is already running, set `"single_instance": false` in the `app` object. Do not pass `--no-single-instance`; Boost rejects it.

### 2. Turn the fake on

`JusPrin2.conf` is JSON:

```json
"jusprin": { "fake_printer": true }
```

An INI `[jusprin]` block is ignored. AppConfig maps JSON booleans to the string `"true"`.

### 3. Real Bambu **system** preset

Select `Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle` (or another BBL system machine). `is_bbl_vendor()` must be true.

Install via **Add a printer…**, or copy `Resources/profiles/BBL` into `<datadir>/system/` and add the A1 mini to the `models` array. Opening `Tape_4_3MF.3mf` only helps **after** that vendor is installed.

### 4. Confirm it switched

In `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log` (use `/usr/bin/grep -a` on this machine; default `grep` may be ugrep):

- `switch_printer_agent: printer agent switched to jusprin-fake-bambu`
- `set_selected_machine=FAKE001`
- later `FakeBambuAgent: connected FAKE001`

If the log says `moonraker` or `orca`, the fake is **not** in the path. Fix the preset. Do not patch UI gates.

The chip shows `Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4` (nickname and nozzle). Idle / Printing / Offline are the **first row of the printer menu**, opened by clicking the printer half of the chip (`SetName("Printer")`). Those words are never on the chip.

### 5. Drive state

Write `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (create `jusprin/` if needed). Reread ~once a second:

```json
{"state":"printing","progress":0.4,"nozzle":210,"bed":60,"offline":false}
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `state` | `idle`, `heating`/`prepare`, `printing`/`running`, `pause`, `finished`, `failed` |
| `progress` | 0–1 → `mc_percent` |
| `nozzle`, `bed` | °C |
| `offline` | `true` stops `push_status`; after ~30 s the menu first row is Offline |

Delete the file, or set `"offline": false` and `"state":"idle"`, to return to Idle.

### 6. Print

Slice, then Print (Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Select Machine lists **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)**. Send completes without a printer. Log: `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, send still succeeds but the menu stays on the file’s state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing walk after send.

### 7. Agents: do not drive the wrong app

Another JusPrin may already be open. On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto’d `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`). Do not `pkill` by name.

Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer chip often has no AX title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use Print’s shortcut. Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events posted that way do not.

### 8. Unit tests

`jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` in a GUI build.

---

Background: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp}` is an in-process
stand-in for a real Bambu printer, used for testing without hardware. It's gated on
by `jusprin.fake_printer` in AppConfig; when on, `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent`
(src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579) substitutes agent id `jusprin-fake-bambu` for
the real `bbl` agent, while keeping a real Bambu Lab system preset selected. Operator
guide: src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md.

What I observed (2026-09-16), testing against a locally built RelWithDebInfo binary
with an isolated scratch --datadir:
1. Enabled fake mode, selected "Bambu Lab A1 mini 0.4 nozzle" system preset, launched
   with tests/data/20mm_cube.obj.
2. Confirmed working: header chip read "Bambu Lab A1 mini · 0.4"; printer-menu first
   row correctly showed Idle, then Printing (after writing
   {"state":"printing",...} to <datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json), then Offline
   (~36s after {"offline":true}) — all matching the README.
3. Sliced the cube, clicked Print, the send dialog correctly listed
   "JusPrin Fake A1 mini(LAN)", clicked Send. The debug log confirmed success:
   `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...3mf dest=`.
4. AFTER that successful send, I reopened the printer-menu (click the printer half
   of the header chip) and it now showed "Not connected" / "Prints go to a card."
   instead of returning to Idle — even though the FakeBambuAgent kept pushing valid
   status in the log the whole time (dev_id=FAKE001, gcode_state=IDLE, no
   disconnect). This never recovered on its own; reopening the menu repeatedly still
   showed "Not connected."

This text comes from src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp:73/76
(`status_word = "Not connected"`, `sub_label = "Prints go to a card."`), which is
presumably driven by src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SetupCommands.cpp's
`printer_connection` (see also SetupCommands.hpp). The commit that introduced this
"Not connected" reporting is a25b95fb39 ("Report a print host's live state in the
printer menu") — but that commit is NOT on jusprin-newui (it lives on
jusprin-newui-fakeprinter / claude/device-simulator-printer-5dee78), so check

commit's message: "a preset without a host, such as one restored from a saved 3mf,
stays 'Not connected' even though the previous machine is still selected in the
device manager" — this smells like the send flow is doing something that makes the
active preset look host-less (e.g. snapshotting/embedding a 3mf-derived preset,
or clearing a print_host field) even though the underlying device connection
(MachineObject/dev_id FAKE001) is still alive.
